title: In one MICrONS mouse, synapses less than 5 µm apart on a shared target show no extra response similarity at fine scale; coarse RF clustering follows source soma positions
abstract: Question: in one MICrONS mouse, do synapses from two imaged source neurons that are close together on a shared target come from neurons with more similar visual responses? Data: public MICrONS v1300 synapses, v1507 cell types and the Ding et al. (2025) response table. We used 736 sources with responses and proofread axons, 289,289 synapses and 37,290 targets with input from at least two sources. Method: for 14,352 pairs of synapses from different sources less than 5 um apart on one target, we compared source similarity with shuffles of source labels on the target: whole target (N1), soma-distance shells (N2, planned primary) and 15 um cubes (N3, added later). We used 1,000 shuffles and a bootstrap over targets. Results: under N3, close pairs had no excess similarity for model signal correlation, response-feature similarity or receptive-field (RF) closeness; all 95% intervals were within 0.014 SD of zero. Under N2, close pairs had closer RFs (+0.058 SD, interval 0.046 to 0.071, p = 0.001). This excess fell with distance up to about 80 um. When we removed the part of RF distance that the soma positions of the sources predict, the excess became zero (+0.0005 SD, interval -0.013 to +0.015). Soma closeness kept a large excess after RF control. Feature similarity, which predicts connections in Ding et al., had at most +0.015 SD under N2 (interval includes zero). Close pairs on one target had more similar sources than close pairs on different targets. This agrees with target-level input preference, not with position on the dendrite. The results held for excitatory and inhibitory targets, core and extended sources, and without the 20 most active sources. Conclusion: these imaged cortical inputs show no functional clustering at a few micrometres. A geometric rule, set by source soma position, explains the coarse RF order. Limits: one mouse; Euclidean, not path, distance; 76% of close pairs on inhibitory targets; unproofread target dendrites; calcium and model-based similarity; N3 and soma-adjusted measures were added after a first look. No record-level data are bundled.
